in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I have a young child, Alex, who's 3 years old and lives with me at home. I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit but wanted to check if I'm eligible first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great that you're checking your eligibility first.

You've mentioned that Alex is 3 years old and lives with you at home, which is a good start. Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

First, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's helpful to know.

Next question: Are you the person responsible for Alex? By this I mean, are you the one who provides for Alex's day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and general care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm responsible for Alex's day-to-day care - I provide for all their needs like food, clothes, and looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very clear.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment. Is Alex currently in any of the following situations:
- In hospital or residential accommodation for an extended period?
- In local authority care?
- Living with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex lives at home with me and isn't in hospital, care, or living with anyone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? (Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually there's a bit of a situation there. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for Alex, and we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. Is that going to be a problem?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that situation. That's an important detail.

According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for the same child. Ideally, you and Alex's other parent should agree between yourselves who will claim it. However, if you cannot agree, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision about who will receive the Child Benefit.

To clarify: has Alex's other parent already submitted a claim for Child Benefit for Alex, or have neither of you claimed yet?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Neither of us has claimed yet. We've been trying to sort out who should claim it, but we haven't been able to agree. So what happens in that situation - can I still apply and let HMRC decide?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct! Even though you haven't reached an agreement, you can still apply for Child Benefit. If both you and Alex's other parent submit claims, HMRC will decide who will receive it based on the circumstances.

Just to complete my assessment, I have a couple of final questions:

1. Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a British citizen, or do you have another immigration status I should know about?

(This helps me confirm there are no residency-related eligibility issues.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, so there shouldn't be any issues with my immigration status.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just one final question to complete the assessment: Are there any other children you're inquiring about for Child Benefit, or is it just Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just Alex. They're my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

Based on all the information you've provided, **you are eligible to apply for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✓ Alex is 3 years old (under 16)  
✓ You live in the UK and are a British citizen  
✓ You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care  
✓ Alex lives with you at home  
✓ Alex is not in hospital, care, or living elsewhere  

**Regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent:** This doesn't prevent you from applying. You can go ahead and submit your claim. If Alex's other parent also submits a claim, HMRC will decide between you based on the circumstances. It's still worth trying to reach an agreement if possible, but the disagreement itself doesn't make you ineligible.

**Next steps:** You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. 

**One thing to keep in mind:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Do you have any other questions about your eligibility or the claiming process?
